original_annotations: Grab the small saucepan from the dishwasher's bottom rack and turn it. [159.19, 160.46]
While holding the small saucepan in my right hand, using my left hand, grab another larger saucepan from the dishwasher bottom rack. [160.56, 161.32]
Stack the small saucepan that I'm holding in my right hand on top of the larger saucepan that I'm holding in my left hand. [161.78, 162.26]
Having changed my mind about stacking the two pans, I put the smaller saucepan that was on top of the stack on the countertop next to the washing machine. [161.45, 164.50]

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the stainless-steel saucepan I was holding. Add one visually matching saucepan to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The released frames show two different silver-coloured saucepans with uncoated-looking silver interiors and broad black handles joined to the pan by short silver necks. Relative size distinguishes the two physical candidates; no legible brand or capacity marking is visible.

The source annotations record separate physical-object tracks for the two saucepans. This is historical annotation evidence, not a capacity measurement from the released pixels; the one-quart value is supplied only by the fixed clarification answer.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent ask a one-slot appearance question before a Candidate Commitment between two visually plausible candidates?
construct.belief_before: Either candidate satisfies the ambiguous request.
construct.required_behavior_change: Resolve the intended physical pan from the fixed answer and leave exactly one matching product in the ending cart; question and early-commitment timing are separate process measures.
construct.no_update_failure: The ending cart contains the wrong physical branch or a product that fails the released matching requirement, or contains missing/extra products. Not asking alone is not an ending-state failure.
construct.overupdate_failure: Keeping both candidate products or another unrequested product leaves extra content in the ending cart; asking in the oracle arm is measured separately.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The scene supplies the silver saucepan body and black-handle appearance that the words steel saucepan and one quart do not specify. The fixed answer resolves relative size and supplies capacity; website details verify that capacity. All-metal and woodgrain handles remain visibly different even when a product is one quart.

answer_boundary_review.selection_rule: Keep the unchanged user instruction and canonical clarification answer; match the scene-visible body/handle appearance and publicly documented quantity/size without inventing brand, coating or exact-instance requirements.
answer_boundary_review.unresolved_candidate_policy: These candidates are not certified rejections; the provisional executable answer set must not be released until their boundary is resolved.
answer_boundary_review.surface_limitations: 原始商品图逐项核查；未对暗光源帧推断精确材质、品牌、容量或细微表面纹理。
answer_boundary_review.required_followup: Resolve the named candidate boundaries, recompile, invalidate only this task, and rerun both independent Coding-Agent passes.

supported_claims.text: The early released frames show two stacked round pans with dark interiors and black handles with silver connector sections. They are separated between the hands in V0:2–V0:4; later frames show the right-hand pan moving into the cupboard. The frames do not establish an exact brand or diameter.

The original source narration describes two piled pans and their separation, and the annotations provide two tracks. Those annotations are historical evidence rather than released narration or a measurement. Relative size comes from the scene; about 20 centimeters is supplied by the fixed clarification answer.
